title: See running processes
summary: A process is a running program. ps shows information about selected processes without stopping them.
introduction: A process is a running program. ps shows information about selected processes without stopping them. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A process is a running program. ps shows information about selected processes without stopping them.
The output lists processes in the current selection, with IDs and commands. The exact list depends on the system.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Find the shell process in the listing.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not stop a process you do not understand, especially on a shared computer.
For more detail later, use this [Linux further reading](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html).

seo.title: Linux: See running processes
seo.description: Learn about see running processes in Linux. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
